normalization.paper_coordinate_description: The paper writes the torus coordinate as zeta = -pi + 2*pi*xi in [-pi,pi), while Appendix A.1 states that the implementation normalizes xi=(x-a_X)/(b_X-a_X) in [0,1] and evaluates Fourier characters exp(2*pi*i*k*xi). These are equivalent periodic coordinates up to an origin shift.
normalization.periodic_lift_seam_note: Appendix A.1 states the linear lifting acts on xi itself rather than on a periodic function of xi, so particles crossing the periodic seam can change lifted features discontinuously.

interpretation.empirical_measure_change: There are two distinct examples: the source-faithful unweighted case adds one equally weighted particle; the weighted extension adds a 1e-12-mass support point while leaving original inlier mass essentially unchanged. The tagged normalization code ignores weights in both cases.
interpretation.normalization_change: The exact NEOPIC arXiv v1 transform independently maps each sample to [0,1]. In either example, support changes from [0.1,0.9] to [0,0.9], shifting every original inlier except the upper endpoint.
interpretation.expected_disposition: Detect and report normalization-induced global coordinate drift separately from sampling / learned-operator error.
interpretation.scope_limit: The normalization formula and [0,1] coordinate interval match the pinned NEOPIC arXiv v1 preprocessing. The paper expresses the same torus coordinate as [-pi,pi) and states that Fourier characters use exp(2*pi*i*k*xi). The source implementation's unweighted sample min/max and per-coordinate application are pinned. This remains a synthetic coordinate/lifting-input witness, not a learned field-output error, kinetic simulation or proof of failure in the published model.

source_faithful_unweighted_case.description: Source-faithful unweighted particle-position sample: every listed particle contributes equally to the empirical measure.
source_faithful_unweighted_case.empirical_measure_note: The unweighted empirical measure changes by adding one of six equally weighted particles and changing the sample count. This case demonstrates native per-sample support sensitivity, not negligible-mass invariance.

weighted_measure_extension.description: Weighted empirical-measure extension. The tagged NEOPIC normalizer still receives only positions and ignores these weights; this case is not claimed to be the paper's native unweighted data interface.
weighted_measure_extension.empirical_measure_note: The added support point has mass 1e-12 and original inlier mass is otherwise preserved (before any optional final mass normalization). The position-only min-max map ignores this mass and remaps all inliers except the upper endpoint.
